comparison: Both support the study design (C18-C23, C27-C30) as appropriate for a first-in-human phase I trial. OpenEval notes limitations of small sample size while peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the novelty without questioning the design.

Both support the manufacturing process (C24-C26, C33-C37). OpenEval raises minor questions about gentamicin use, while peer reviewers explicitly endorse the approach of sourcing cells from healthy upper lobes as contributing to safety.

Both address cell morphology correlations (C38-C40). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to small sample size and lack of mechanistic explanation, while peer reviewers accept these exploratory findings without challenge.

Both support the single-cell sequencing characterization (C41-C49). OpenEval finds the data well-supported though therapeutic contribution remains speculative. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse the RNASeq evidence that cells are not fibrogenic.

Both support comparisons showing cells differ from pro-fibrotic populations (C50-C52, C91-C95). OpenEval notes functional consequences remain to be demonstrated, while peer reviewers accept this as evidence supporting safety claims.

Both support safety findings (C53-C65, C97-C98, C113). OpenEval notes some AE attributions are subjective and COVID-19 complicates interpretation. Peer reviewers provide strong endorsement, stating 'convincing evidence' of safety and supporting Phase 2 progression.

Both rate DLCO efficacy claims (C67-C69) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval cites small sample size, no placebo control, COVID-19 confounding, and concomitant medications. Peer reviewers strongly emphasize that efficacy cannot be concluded from Phase 1 without placebo control, requiring Phase 2 validation.

Both rate FVC efficacy claims (C72-C75) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval questions clinical significance of minimal changes and notes multiple confounders. Peer reviewers maintain efficacy conclusions require placebo-controlled validation and advise further softening of claims.

Both rate functional outcome improvements (C76-C80) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are secondary endpoints in uncontrolled trial with potential placebo effects. Peer reviewers emphasize only safety findings are robust without placebo group.

Both rate CT imaging improvements (C83-C88, C115) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes remarkable findings in only 2 patients with concerns about lack of blinded assessment and contradictions with morphology correlations. Peer reviewers acknowledge improvements as encouraging but requiring Phase 2 validation for efficacy claims.

Both support acknowledgment of COVID-19 confounding (C70, C111). OpenEval identifies this as major limitation undermining dose-response assessment. Peer reviewers accept this limitation as consistent with need for controlled Phase 2 studies.

Both support concomitant medication reporting (C31-C32, C120). OpenEval notes Nintedanib exclusion creates potential confounding. Peer reviewers accept the medication use and exclusion rationale without challenge.

Both support acknowledgment of study limitations (C108-C110). OpenEval notes authors are appropriately transparent. Peer reviewers strongly emphasize these limitations, with editor and anonymous reviewer stating limitations section should be more forthright about inability to claim efficacy.

Both support need for Phase 2 investigation (C112). OpenEval notes this is appropriate for addressing limitations. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse Phase 2 progression, stating improvements warrant further study and Phase 2 will be the time to claim efficacy.

OpenEval rates historical control comparisons (C103-C107) as UNSUPPORTED due to confounding by pirfenidone use and lack of concurrent controls. Peer reviewers rate DLCO/efficacy claims (partially overlapping C106-C107) as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing need for placebo control rather than specifically challenging historical comparisons.
OpenEval supports background claims about IPF clinical context (C1-C6) as appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval supports prior literature on P63+ cell biology (C7-C12) establishing study rationale. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval supports prior preclinical/clinical work citations (C13-C17) providing scientific foundation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval supports literature context claims (C89-C90, C96) establishing rationale for cell therapy in IPF. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports main conclusion (C116) as appropriately cautious for Phase 1, noting safety is well-supported but efficacy is tentative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers' overall stance aligns with this assessment.
